question:
(a) Explain the role of internal resistance of a cell in an electric circuit.
(b) Obtain the expression for current drawn from a cell of emf $\varepsilon$ and internal resistance $r$ connected to an external resistance $R$.
(c) A cell of emf $6\,\text{V}$ and internal resistance $1\,\Omega$ is connected to an external resistance of $5\,\Omega$. Calculate the current in the circuit.

options.A:
(a) Internal resistance is the opposition offered only by the external circuit.
(b) $I=\dfrac{\varepsilon}{R-r}$.
(c) $I=\dfrac{6}{5-1}=1.5\,\text{A}$.
options.B:
(a) Internal resistance is opposition within the cell due to its electrolyte and electrodes; it causes internal drop and makes terminal voltage less than emf when current flows.
(b) $\varepsilon=IR+Ir=I(R+r)$, so $I=\dfrac{\varepsilon}{R+r}$.
(c) $I=\dfrac{6}{5+1}=1\,\text{A}$.
options.C:
(a) Internal resistance is zero for all cells.
(b) $I=\dfrac{R+r}{\varepsilon}$.
(c) $I=\dfrac{6}{30}=0.2\,\text{A}$.
options.D:
(a) Internal resistance affects only the emf and not terminal potential difference.
(b) $I=\dfrac{\varepsilon}{Rr}$.
(c) $I=\dfrac{6}{5}=1.2\,\text{A}$.
